description: Making liquid tree in space station
summary: We developed a self-assembled backup system for a sealed station. This solution addresses the challenge of oxygen depletion and carbon dioxide CO2 buildup, which occurs over time as the crew consumes oxygen and exhales CO2. This backup system is critically important because if the primary life support fails, the crew is left with a limited amount of time, making a self-assembled alternative essential.
details:
Our project is an emergency backup life-support system designed for a sealed station. It works by addressing oxygen depletion and carbon dioxide (CO2) buildup, which occur over time as the crew consumes oxygen and exhales CO2.
The primary benefit of this solution is crew self-reliance during critical emergencies, as the system is specifically designed so the crew can assemble it themselves. Because a primary life-support failure leaves the crew with strictly limited time, the intended impact of our project is to safeguard the crew when main systems fail.
In designing this project, our team carefully considered the constraints of a sealed environment, the continuous accumulation of exhaled CO2, and the urgent time limits faced during a system failure, ensuring the backup can be assembled directly by the crew.
